journal.text: Day 1 setup: I bought a diversified core of large-cap tech and AI names plus semiconductors, and I tilted it toward stocks with strong momentum over the last 60 days. Those leaders are GOOGL (313, up from 245 in early October), MU (285, up from 186), AMAT, KLAC, LRCX and ASML. For balance I added defensive holdings in WMT and COST. I skipped TSLA, PLTR and NFLX: TSLA and PLTR had been falling late in December, and NFLX was in a steady downtrend (124 down to 94). About $47k is invested and about $3k is kept as cash. Plan: add the monthly $50k deposit in Feb, weighted toward the names with the strongest trends. Rebalance if any position falls more than 15% below its entry price or becomes more than 15% of the portfolio. Revisit semis if MU, KLAC or LRCX break below their mid-December lows.

None of these moves comes close to my rebalance rules. My Day 1 note mentions AMAT, but I don't hold it; I could add it in February. I'm keeping about $3k in cash. Plan is unchanged: put the Feb $50k deposit into the names with the strongest trends. I'll reconsider a position if it drops more than 15% below cost or becomes more than 15% of the portfolio. I'll also revisit the semis if MU, KLAC or LRCX break below their mid-December lows.

So I'm diversifying into new positions: AMGN $5k, PEP $4k, AEP $4k, CSX $4k, TMUS $4k, GILD $3k and AMAT $4k. About $30k in cash stays back for later tranches over the next 1–2 weeks, either to add to the new names on pullbacks or to buy tech if it stabilizes.
